source_refs.note: Book p. 205: 11.4 Values of Trigonometric Functions: the 12 identities for -theta, pi-theta, pi+theta, 2pi-theta and the list of angle measures they give (-30 to +/-360 degrees).

blocks.text: We know the values of trigonometric functions for angles of measure \(0^{\circ}\), \(30^{\circ}\), \(45^{\circ}\), \(60^{\circ}\) and \(90^{\circ}\). We have also established the following identities:

blocks.title: Teaching note

blocks.text: By using the above identities, we can easily find the values of trigonometric functions of the angles of the following measures:

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
The method is always the same three steps:
1. Write the angle as \(-\theta\), \(180^{\circ} - \theta\), \(180^{\circ} + \theta\) or \(360^{\circ} - \theta\), where \(\theta\) is one of \(0^{\circ}, 30^{\circ}, 45^{\circ}, 60^{\circ}, 90^{\circ}\).
2. Use the matching identity from the table to change the function of the big angle into the same function of \(\theta\), with a sign.
3. Put in the known value for \(\theta\).
Why we need this now: the graphs in 11.4.2 to 11.4.4 are drawn from tables of values at \(0^{\circ}, 30^{\circ}, 60^{\circ}, \dots, 360^{\circ}\) and at negative angles. Every entry of those tables comes from these identities.

blocks.caption: Values at the basic angles (our summary table, to keep beside you; decimals rounded to two places)

blocks.text: Worked values (our practice, not printed in the book)

items: \(\tan(-315^{\circ}) = -\tan 315^{\circ} = -\tan(360^{\circ} - 45^{\circ}) = -(-\tan 45^{\circ}) = 1\). Why: first \(\tan(-\theta) = -\tan\theta\), then \(\tan(2\pi - \theta) = -\tan\theta\); two minus signs make a plus.

blocks.title: Exam tip
blocks.text: Check every answer with the quadrant: \(240^{\circ}\) is in Quadrant III, where cosine is negative, so \(\cos 240^{\circ}\) must be negative. If your sign disagrees with the quadrant, you used the wrong identity.

blocks.title: Key points
blocks.text:
1. Only the values at \(0^{\circ}, 30^{\circ}, 45^{\circ}, 60^{\circ}, 90^{\circ}\) need to be remembered.
2. The twelve identities of the table turn any of the listed angles into one of these basic angles.
3. For \(\pi \pm \theta\), \(2\pi - \theta\) and \(-\theta\) the function stays the same; only the sign can change.
4. The sign follows the quadrant of the angle.
5. These values fill the tables used to draw the graphs in the next sub-sections.

blocks.title: Common mistake
blocks.text:
1. Writing \(\cos(\pi - \theta) = \cos\theta\): the cosine of an angle in Quadrant II is negative, so \(\cos(\pi - \theta) = -\cos\theta\).
2. Forgetting the outer minus sign for negative angles: \(\tan(-315^{\circ}) = -\tan 315^{\circ}\), and then \(\tan 315^{\circ}\) itself is negative.
3. Mixing up \(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\) and \(\frac{1}{2}\): sine grows with the angle in Quadrant I, so \(\sin 60^{\circ}\) is the bigger one.
